meta.purpose: Parameters for an MBTI-style layer derived from Big Five (TIPI) z-scores. The app does not administer the MBTI.
meta.sign_convention: MBTI continuous scores run E->I, S->N, T->F, J->P (as in McCrae & Costa 1989). A POSITIVE correlation or weight means MORE of the SECOND letter: positive EI = more Introverted, positive SN = more iNtuitive, positive TF = more Feeling, positive JP = more Perceiving. N in the Big Five keys is Neuroticism (reverse of TIPI Emotional Stability).
meta.status_tags: verified = read from the source or a reputable reproduction this session; derived = our arithmetic; unverified = not checked, do not quote.

EI.status: verified via two secondary reproductions of the table (original paywalled)

women_n201.note: Only cells significant at p<.05 were available; null = not significant, exact value unverified.

pooled_n468.note: (267*men + 201*women)/468 for cells retained in the model. derived.

FMC2003.finding: Abstract: E with EI, O with SN, A with TF, C with JP, replicating MC1989.

F2022.status: verified as printed; scoring direction unclear and pattern contradicts earlier work. NOT used.

other_studies.meta_analysis: None found for MBTI x Big Five correlations.

recommended_model.formula: P(second letter | z) = Phi((sum_k w_k * z_k - cut) / residual_sd); P(first letter) = 1 - that. z_k are Big Five z-scores against a general adult norm (N = neuroticism = -emotional stability). Closest type = more probable letter on each dichotomy. P(type) ~= product of the four letter probabilities (assumes conditional independence).
recommended_model.cut_formula: cut = Phi^-1(1 - population share of second letter); 0 for a median split.

tipi_attenuation.explanation: sqrt of TIPI 6-week retest reliability (E .77, A .71, C .76, ES .70, O .62; G2003 Table 3). Shrinks NEO-based weights because TIPI is a noisier measure. Our modelling choice.

EI.explanation: Low Extraversion drives I; Neuroticism adds a little (significant in both sexes). -.72*.877=-.632; .16*.837=.134; R2=.399+.018.

SN.explanation: Openness drives N; Extraversion adds a little (pooled .15). The cut is far from the median because only ~27% are N.

TF.explanation: Agreeableness drives F; low Conscientiousness and (mainly in women) Neuroticism add a little. Weakest mapping: Big Five explain under 20% of TF, so probabilities stay close to the base rate.

JP.explanation: Low Conscientiousness drives P; Openness and Extraversion add to P (both significant in both sexes).

assumptions: Zero-order correlations used as regression weights (exact only if Big Five domains are uncorrelated).
Single 1989 US sample, older MBTI form.
MBTI scales treated as conditionally independent for the 16-type probability.
Cells kept if significant in both sexes or pooled |r| >= .15.

letter_prevalence.source: MBTI1998 US national representative sample, as reproduced in PC2008 Table 13

type_prevalence.note: Sums to 100.3 through rounding in the source.

OPP2011.note: participants already knew their type; upper bound

critics_secondhand.McCarley_Carskadon_1983: 50% changed on at least one scale at 5 weeks

flip_model.same_letter_share: 0.5 + asin(r)/pi for a median cut with retest correlation r
flip_model.flip_probability: Phi(-r*d/sqrt(1-r^2)) for a person d SD from the cut

lifespan_implication.note: Average person, TIPI weights, US cut, using app's normative Big Five shifts age 20->70 (C +0.82, N -0.77, A +0.41, E +0.15, O -0.03 SD; reconstructed from RWV2006 in model_params.json). Requires z-scores against a fixed adult norm.
lifespan_implication.direct_mbti_evidence: Cummings 1995: significant age-group differences on every MBTI dimension (directions unverified). No verified study on upbringing or life events and MBTI change.
